artifacts.summary: Confirms every mcp.py invocation shape (stdio server, --briefing-text, --receipt, --effect-line) resolves the token from ~/.sapience/config.json via one shared module-level line with SAPIENCE_TOKEN unset; recommends dropping the token branch from setup-sapience-mcp.sh's generate_sapience_config(), inverting verify-sapience-mcp.sh check (b), adding a negative-control regression test, documenting token locations/copy-boundary in per-repo-scoping.md, and flags an unrelated dead dotfiles-repo writer as a non-blocking follow-up.

memory_candidates.content: ~/.sapience/mcp.py resolves its credential via a single module-level statement (TOKEN = os.environ.get('SAPIENCE_TOKEN') or _CFG.get('token') or '') executed once at import, before any sys.argv/CLI-flag dispatch. Every invocation shape (bare stdio server, --briefing-text, --receipt, --effect-line, --statusline, etc.) therefore resolves the token identically and falls back to ~/.sapience/config.json when the env var is unset -- there is no per-flag divergence to audit separately. os.path.expanduser('~') also resolves via the passwd database when HOME is unset, so this fallback is robust even in a stripped spawn environment.

~/.dotfiles/packages/sapience-flake/lib/wrappers.nix defines sapience-register-mcp (backed by a passing Nix check, checks/register-mcp.nix) that writes SAPIENCE_TOKEN into a TOP-LEVEL ~/.claude.json .mcpServers.sapience entry when a token is resolvable. grepping modules/home/services/sapience.nix for any reference to this wrapper (wrappers., register-mcp, sapienceRegisterMcp) returns nothing -- it is not invoked by the home-manager module actually applied on this machine, consistent with setup-sapience-mcp.sh's own header note that the former machine-wide sapienceMcpServer/registerMcpServer option has been retired. It is dead code today but would reintroduce a token-bearing entry if ever re-wired.

setup-sapience-mcp.sh's process_write() already does whole-entry (never per-field) comparison and replacement of the per-project MCP registration entry. This means any future change to the canonical entry shape (e.g. dropping a field) self-migrates every existing registered entry on the very next writer invocation (the SessionStart hook calls the writer unconditionally for an active repo) with zero additional migration code -- a divergent existing entry is simply judged non-canonical and replaced wholesale.
